title: Programming in Python II: data, algorithms and simulations
audience: a high-school student (grades 9–12) or an adult reviewing high-school work
purpose: Write well-structured Python programs that use functions, lists, strings, dictionaries, sets and files; test them with assert; design and compare algorithms for searching, sorting and counting; write simulations; and discuss the effects of computing on society, at the level of AP Computer Science Principles.

weeks.3: Lists in depth: slicing, methods and comprehensions
weeks.8: Sorting: selection sort, insertion sort and sorted()
weeks.11: Data, privacy and the impact of computing
weeks.12: Program design: planning a larger program

blocks.deliverable: Week 7 midterm; compare two searches by counting steps.
Submit the project; take an unseen 60 minute final in week 14.

project: Data explorer: write a program that loads a supplied data set, computes summaries with dictionaries, answers five questions about the data with functions, includes tests, and reports its findings with a short note on privacy.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
